items.title: Architecture of Attention
items.desc: A two-hour keynote rebuilt from the script up. We treated each act as a film: cold open, escalation, payoff. Every transition earned its keep.

items.title: Signal in the noise
items.desc: A festival identity built around one idea: every performance, one signal. We directed the live show, the visuals, and the morning-after recap film.

items.title: A film for an opening
items.desc: A campaign film built in nine shots. No voiceover. No music sting at the end. Just a room, a window, and a guest.

items.title: Generative pipeline, in production
items.desc: A production pipeline mixing generative imagery with directed photography. Built so the human stays in the room.

items.title: Concert visuals, residency
items.desc: Eight nights, one visual language, no two shows the same. The visuals listened to the room.

items.title: Brand activation, museum night
items.desc: A late-night activation that turned the permanent collection into a stage. Press loved it. So did the security guards.

items.title: Keynote, in three acts
items.desc: A founder who hated keynotes, asked to do one. We wrote the script first, then the deck, then the stage. He still hates them. This one worked.

items.title: Festival recap, six minutes
items.desc: Edited from 60+ hours of footage. The cut you remember the next morning, not the one that won the algorithm.

items.title: Stage design, corporate launch
items.desc: Hard problem: a product launch in a venue with no theatre rigging and a 90-minute load-in. The stage was the film.

items.title: Manifesto, one page
items.desc: One page. 240 words. The founder reads it before every all-hands. That was the brief.
